brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 life-moment evites: baby shower, gender reveal, bridal shower, engagement, graduation, sweet 16, quinceañera, retirement, farewell, celebration of life, reunion, housewarming.
brief.audience: Every generation; the celebration of life must hold grief gently.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
Quinceañera is culturally specific: collaboration-gated, specific and respectful.

proposals.title: The Measure of the Moment
proposals.idea: Every evite is governed by a single proportional canon — a golden-section armature derived from the event's emotional register — from which type scale, foreground plane spacing, foil vector, and motion timing all descend without exception, so that the celebration's hierarchy is felt before a word is read.
proposals.geometry: A vertical golden rectangle (1 : 1.618) rules the artboard at 390 px wide; a nine-field harmonic grid (three columns, three rows weighted 1 : 2 : 1 horizontally, 1 : 3 : 1 vertically) places the primary image in the dominant field and live text in the secondary. Each of the twelve events is assigned a cantus-firmus angle between 0° and 45° in 3.75° steps — baby shower 0°, graduation 15°, retirement 33.75°, celebration of life 11.25°, and so on — and that angle alone determines foil-highlight vector, foreground drift axis, bokeh origin offset, and the sequential plane-arrival order. Nothing floats free of the measure.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) carries all event titles — optical size Large, tracked −10 to −20 per event's emotional weight (tighter for grief, looser for joy). Cormorant SC sets the date-time line at 11 px, full caps, tracking +200. EB Garamond handles body venue copy at 14 px regular. No sans-serif except a single instance of Josefin Sans (OFL) for the host name line, providing one counterpoint interval the way a passing tone resolves. Scale ratio across the hierarchy is exactly 1 : 1.333 (perfect fourth), matching the proportional system.
proposals.imageLogic: Twelve Magnific prompt grids — one per event, each returning 8–16 plates — are directed as architectural still lifes: a shaft of physically motivated light enters from the cantus-firmus angle, strikes a single material object that carries the event's meaning (a linen-wrapped bassinet, a mortarboard on marble, an open door at dusk, a candle in a darkened room for the celebration of life). No people; presence is implied by object and light. Plates are composited as the deep background layer; foreground cut-outs — a botanical sprig, a ribbon curl, a dried petal — are generated separately as PNG assets on transparency, sized to the golden-section subordinate fields. All plates are desaturated 15% and cooled 200K so the WebGL foil layer reads as the warmest element in the image.
proposals.texture: Simulated cotton-rag paper tooth is baked into the art plate via a Magnific texture pass — visible as micro-grain at 1:1 pixel scale, invisible at arm's length — so the evite reads as a physical object. Foil is a WebGL specular highlight map locked to the cantus-firmus light vector; it catches only the title letterforms and one material edge in the art plate. Film grain shader at 4% opacity runs continuously at 24 fps; reduced-motion flag drops it to a static grain bake. No glitter, no confetti scatter — those are decorative without structural consequence.
proposals.motion: Plane arrival is sequential and metered: art plate fades in over 600 ms (ease-out cubic), foreground cut-outs drift into position along the cantus-firmus axis over 800 ms with a 120 ms stagger between planes, foil highlight cross-fades in at 1200 ms. Phone-tilt parallax runs at ±6 px on the foreground layer, ±2 px on the art plate — a narrow interval that implies depth without destabilising the grid. The celebration of life suppresses all tilt response by default (reduced motion honoured doubly for grief); its only motion is a single candle-flicker shader, 0.3 Hz, amplitude ±3% luminance, which is the quietest thing the system can do. Total load sequence resolves in under 1.4 s. Nothing moves after resolution unless the guest tilts — the frame holds.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific batch prompt per event (twelve total, two submission rounds) specifies: motivated light angle matching the cantus-firmus value, single hero object, cotton-rag surface, no faces, physically plausible shadow. Foreground cut-outs are a second Magnific pass on transparent PNG — botanical and object elements only. WebGL layer is a GLSL shader authored procedurally: specular highlight map keyed to the locked light vector, bokeh pass keyed to the same origin, grain pass. Tela document structure: Layer 1 art plate, Layer 2 foreground PNGs (drift-enabled), Layer 3 WebGL mask, Layer 4 live text. No photography, no physical build, no commissioned illustration. Editorial selection of the best 2–3 plates per event from each batch is the human act.
proposals.humanTrace: The cantus-firmus angle for each event was set by a human judgment about emotional register before any image existed — that prior constraint, and the editorial eye that selected which generated plate best answered it, is the perceptible sign of making. The grain and paper-tooth passes simulate the pressure of a hand-laid sheet; the foil vector simulates the decision a bookbinder makes about where light should catch. The system is generative; the governing decisions are not.
proposals.risk: The strict proportional canon risks feeling ceremonial where an event wants warmth — a baby shower governed by golden-section mathematics may read as cold to a parent who wanted something soft. That risk is worth taking because the alternative, twelve independently art-directed evites with no common structural logic, produces a product line that cannot be recognised as a system, and a system that cannot be read as a system cannot be trusted with the moments people remember. The measure is not coldness; it is the reason a cathedral and a lullaby both feel inevitable.

proposals.title: Ink Pulled, Moment Fixed
proposals.idea: Every evite is a ghost of a physical print run — generative ink bleed, registration drift, and torn-edge masks make the phone screen feel like it just came off the press, so the moment lands with the weight of something made by a body for a specific person.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 card; a single dominant bleed plate bleeds to all four edges with no safe white margin — the image is the card; foreground cut-outs float on a second plane at ±6% tilt offset; text lives in a narrow 24px left-margin gutter ruled like a printer's gripper edge, not centred; the QR is letterpress-stamped in the bottom-right corner as a design element, not an afterthought; link preview crops to the top 52% of the plate, so the dominant mark always survives the thumbnail
proposals.typography: Heading: Space Grotesk (OFL, Google Fonts) set in all-caps, tracking +120, size 28–34px, reversed out of the plate in a deliberately imperfect ink-dropout mask — letters look pulled from a linocut, not typeset on a screen; secondary: Space Grotesk Regular 14px, tracking +40, left-aligned in the gutter; date/venue: Courier Prime (OFL) 11px, monospace register-mark feel; NO script, NO serif for this direction — script is what every competitor does
proposals.imageLogic: One Magnific prompt batch per event type returns 12 distinct generative art plates in a single grid call; each plate is directed as a simulated relief print: deep-ink ground colour, one dominant gestural mark (a pulled squeegee arc, a torn stencil shape, a monoprint ghost), visible paper tooth rendered as fine-grain noise at 4% opacity, and a colour bleed halo at the mark edge; plates are NOT photographs of events — they are abstract emotional registers of the moment; baby shower: cadmium yellow ground, soft circular bleed, second-pull ghost; celebration of life: deep indigo ground, single white candle-flame monoprint mark, heavy grain, no confetti, no flowers — grief held in the negative space around the mark; quinceañera plate: collaboration-gated — directed only after community sign-off, inspired by papel picado geometry and Oaxacan textile colour logic, specific and attributable, not
proposals.texture: Generative paper tooth simulated via Magnific noise pass at 4% over every plate; ink bleed at mark edges rendered as gaussian + directional blur composite in the shader layer; registration drift: foreground cut-out layer offset by 2–3px in a single axis, colour-shifted to simulate a second-pass misregistration; torn edge masks on cut-out layer use a procedural fractal-edge shader — ragged, not die-cut smooth; WebGL foil shimmer applies ONLY along the torn edge of the dominant mark, not flood-filled — it earns its place by proving the mark was there first
proposals.motion: Sequence is fast, physical, press-like — (1) plate slams in at 0ms, full bleed, 180ms ease-out — no fade, a hit; (2) registration-drift layer slides 3px left then settles to final position over 220ms, simulating a second pass; (3) torn-edge foil shimmer activates along mark edges only, driven by tilt gyroscope — when phone tilts, foil tracks; (4) foreground cut-outs drift on gyroscope at ±6% parallax, slower than foil — two distinct depth planes; (5) text fades in last at 400ms, letter-spacing collapses from +240 to +120 over 160ms, like ink being pressed into paper; reduced-motion fallback: static plate, no shimmer, no drift, all text visible at frame 0 — no information lost
proposals.productionMethod: Single Magnific batch prompt: '12 abstract relief-print plates, one per life moment [list], simulated linocut/monoprint aesthetic, deep ink grounds, single dominant gestural mark per plate, paper tooth grain, ink bleed halo at mark edges, no photography, no illustration of people, pure abstract mark-making, colour palette per moment [list], 9:19.5 portrait, 1080×2340px each, flat-cost grid return'; shader pass adds registration drift and fractal torn-edge mask procedurally in Tela's WebGL layer; foil shimmer mapped to mark-edge mask extracted from plate; foreground cut-outs are Plajah-owned 3D asset renders (botanicals, ribbons, geometric solids) composited transparent PNG with gyro drift; all text live in Tela — never baked
proposals.humanTrace: The registration drift — that 2–3px offset of the second colour pass — is the trace; it is a decision about where a press failed to hold, made before any prompt is written, and every element on screen is accountable to it; the torn edge is not decorative, it is the record of the mask being pulled; the foil only appears where the mark already tore, so the shimmer proves the tear came first
proposals.risk: Guests expecting floral watercolour or gold-script evites will open this and see an abstract mark; some will not immediately read it as celebratory — that three-second delay of recognition is the risk and it is worth it because the moment they resolve it, the card is memorable in a way no floral template ever is; the celebration of life plate risks feeling too spare — a single white mark on indigo with no softening gesture — but grief is spare, and prettifying it is the greater failure

proposals.title: State-Change Invitations
proposals.idea: Each evite is a physical simulation, not a decorated card — a declared light source, a depth-plane contract, and a single generative rule that makes every shimmer, particle drift, and parallax offset a derivable consequence of the event's emotional physics.
proposals.geometry: Each plate is a portrait 9:19.5 viewport (390×844px logical). Three explicit depth planes: background field (z=0), mid-plane cut-outs (z=1, parallax gain ×1.8), foreground micro-elements (z=2, gain ×3.2). Light source declared per event as a polar coordinate (azimuth °, elevation °) baked into the batch prompt — that single declaration propagates to foil shimmer angle, bokeh falloff origin, shadow offset on cut-outs, and particle emission direction. No event shares a light position. Grid structure within each plate is determined by the event's emotional axis: vertical rise (graduation, quinceañera, sweet 16), radial bloom (baby shower, gender reveal, celebration of life), horizontal threshold-crossing (farewell, retirement, housewarming, reunion), and oblique tension (engagement, bridal shower — two vectors converging). Text sits in a reserved live zone: upper 18% for host/event name, lo
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — variable weight axis exploited so the event name renders at weight 300 for grief-adjacent events (celebration of life, farewell) and 700 for kinetic ones (graduation, sweet 16, quinceañera). Secondary: DM Sans (OFL) at 13px/1.6 line-height for all metadata, all-lowercase, tracked +0.04em. No decorative script faces — the foil WebGL layer provides the luxury signal, not the letterform. Size contract: event name 32–40px responsive clamp, never smaller than 28px at 390px. Reduced-motion fallback: weight stays static at 500.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. All plates are Magnific-generated art. One master batch prompt structured as a 12-cell instruction grid, each cell specifying: subject matter, depth-plane content per z-layer, declared light source (polar), color temperature (warm/cool/neutral), and one dominant material system (see texture). The prompt directs Magnific to return plates at 2048×4096px with deliberate seams between depth layers marked by luminance discontinuities — these seams are the cut lines for foreground extraction in Tela. A second Magnific pass generates 8–16 micro-element variants per event (petals, ribbon ends, smoke wisps, confetti vectors, leaf fragments) as isolated objects on black for multiply-blend foreground layers. The AI is directed, not browsed: every prompt specifies the light source polar coordinate first, before subject.
proposals.texture: Each event owns a primary material system that drives the WebGL layer behavior: Baby shower → translucent latex membrane (subsurface scatter, soft bokeh, no hard specular). Gender reveal → compressed-smoke fluid sim (particle emission burst, color temperature flip on interaction). Bridal shower → pressed botanical on vellum (grain, diffuse foil at 12° shimmer). Engagement → molten glass surface (high-specular foil, caustic light leak from declared source). Graduation → embossed archival paper (deep relief normal map, gold foil at 45° upper-right). Sweet 16 → iridescent mylar (full-spectrum shimmer, fast parallax response). Quinceañera → hand-embroidered textile simulation (thread-path normal map, warm candle flicker — collaboration-gated, developed with cultural consultant before any prompt is written). Retirement → patinated brass and linen (low shimmer, slow bokeh drift). Farewell → wa
proposals.motion: Motion is governed by three input states: idle, gyro-tilt, and scroll-entry. Entry sequence is identical for all 12 (system coherence): background plate fades from 0→100% opacity over 400ms ease-out; mid-plane cut-outs drift in from their parallax-zero position over 600ms with 80ms stagger per element; foreground micro-elements arrive last at 800ms. Idle state: micro-elements oscillate on a Lissajous path (amplitude 3px, period 4–7s, randomized per element) — this is not a loop, it is a continuous low-frequency simulation. Gyro-tilt: parallax gain applied per plane (z=0 gain 0, z=1 gain ×1.8, z=2 gain ×3.2) — the light source highlight on the foil layer shifts by (tilt_x × 0.4°, tilt_y × 0.4°), remaining consistent with the declared light source polar. Event-specific motion: candle-flicker shader active only for celebration of life and retirement (2–8Hz flicker, warm color temperature os
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific batch prompt runs. Prompt 1: 12-cell structured instruction, each cell beginning with 'light source [azimuth]° [elevation]°' — returns 12 background plates at 2048×4096px. Editorial pass selects strongest per event. Prompt 2: micro-element grids, 8–16 objects per event on black ground, used for foreground extraction via luminance mask in Tela. WebGL layer: written as a single modular shader with event-type flags (foil, bokeh, candle, particle, caustic) toggled per Tela document — one codebase, 12 configurations. Depth-plane extraction uses the luminance seam strategy from Prompt 1; no manual masking. All motion parameters (Lissajous frequency, parallax gain, shimmer angle) are JSON-configurable per event document, derived from the light source declaration. Quinceañera plate is held until cultural consultation is complete — a placeholder ships first.
proposals.humanTrace: The light source declaration. Every downstream parameter is a consequence of a choice a human made: writing '210° azimuth, 35° elevation' into a prompt cell is a directed act of physical reasoning, not a filter selection. The editorial pass — choosing which of 12 Magnific returns best honors the event's emotional physics — is a curatorial judgment. The shader flag configuration per event is a systems-design decision. The human trace is the architecture of constraints, not a gestural mark.
proposals.risk: This direction risks reading as cold or technical to users who associate celebration with warmth and decoration. The bet is that physically coherent behavior — a highlight that moves correctly when you tilt the phone, a candle flicker that breathes rather than loops, a parallax that feels like depth rather than a trick — produces an emotional response that surface decoration cannot, because it feels real. The celebration of life is the highest-stakes test: grief requires warmth, and a simulation must earn that warmth through material choice (candlelight, aged paper, slow bokeh) rather than sentimentality. If the system logic is invisible to users and the result feels alive, the risk is worth it.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a reveal moment — a dramatic transition, a flourish, a crescendo. I expect a proposal for event-specific entrance animations that are spectacular in isolation but inconsistent as a system. proposals.title: Fieldwork for the Living
proposals.idea: Each evite is a hand-assembled field document — a specific place on earth photographed from above or at ground level, layered with the material culture of that life-moment's actual geography, so a quinceañera in Oaxaca looks nothing like one in Guadalajara and a celebration of life feels like a letter kept in a drawer.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 base, subdivided by a field-notebook grid: one large bleed-edge plate (full width, ~62% of height) above a ruled lower panel that holds live text — the ruled lines are visible, slightly irregular, 1.5px warm gray, generated to look pressed rather than drawn. Foreground cut-outs float in the upper plate zone only. No symmetry enforced; each card tips 1–3° off axis to simulate a photograph placed on a surface rather than centered in a frame.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — variable-weight, set tight, mixed case, never all-caps; it carries the weight of an old letter without costuming. Secondary / data fields (name, date, venue): DM Mono (OFL) at 11–13px, tracking +80, used like a typewriter annotation. Scale contrast is extreme: event title at 52–60px optical, venue line at 12px. No decorative scripts — the emotion lives in the image, not the letterform.
proposals.imageLogic: All art plates generated via Magnific prompt grid — one prompt batch yields 8–16 distinct plates per event type. Prompt architecture specifies: (1) a real, named geographic starting point relevant to the moment (a coastal estuary for a baby shower; late-afternoon light in a specific named city for retirement); (2) a physical material layer — indigo-dyed linen for bridal, pressed botanicals for celebration of life, hand-embroidered textile close-up for quinceañera (Zapotec-specific, collaboration-gated — this plate is held pending community partnership); (3) a motivated single light source, angle specified in degrees, consistent across all foreground cut-out composites and WebGL foil masks for that card. Foreground cut-outs are generatively isolated objects — a single calla lily stem, a worn leather-bound book, a small clay vessel — each photographically plausible, never illustrated. No s
proposals.texture: Simulated analog surface per event type: baby shower — soft-grain watercolor paper with visible cold-press tooth; bridal shower — linen weave with slight warp irregularity; quinceañera — woven textile surface, color palette drawn from Zapotec backstrap-loom geometry (held for collaboration gate); graduation — matte uncoated stock with a faint letterpress deboss halo around the headline; celebration of life — aged vellum, translucent edge-bleed, no shimmer, no foil — grief does not glitter; sweet 16 / gender reveal — glassine over a color field, light refraction; reunion — topographic map paper, fine contour lines; housewarming — raw plaster with a trowel-mark texture. WebGL foil shimmer is masked to material-plausible zones only (a ribbon, a seal, a border thread) and inherits the single motivated light angle — foil highlight direction is locked to the same vector as the plate's key ligh
proposals.motion: Three-phase sequence, total ≤ 4 seconds on first open, then idle: (1) 0–0.8s — plate fades up from overexposed white, emulating a photograph developing; (2) 0.8–2.2s — foreground cut-outs drift in from slight offset positions, parallax-ready, settling with a 12-frame ease-out that reads as weight, not bounce; (3) 2.2–4s — WebGL layer wakes: foil shimmer traces the motivated light vector slowly left to right, bokeh particles (if present) rise at 0.3px/frame, candle flicker (celebration of life only) at 24fps irregular interval. Tilt response: phone gyroscope drives foreground cut-out parallax ±6px on X/Y — slow, physical, no spring overshoot. Celebration of life: tilt range halved to ±3px, no shimmer, candle flicker is the only live element — motion is grief-paced. Reduced-motion: plate fades up, cut-outs appear static at final position, no parallax, no shimmer pulse — card reads as a sti
proposals.productionMethod: Magnific batch prompt — two rounds: Round 1 produces 16 plates across all 12 event types (some types get 2 variants for A/B); prompt specifies exact light angle (e.g., '35° upper-left key, warm 3200K, hard edge'), material surface, geographic anchor, and negative space zone for text panel. Round 2 refines the top plate per type with upscale and texture pass. Foreground cut-outs generated as isolated objects on neutral ground, then composited in Tela with blend-mode multiply or screen depending on surface. WebGL shader receives the motivated light angle as a uniform — one float, set per card, propagating through foil highlight direction, bokeh scatter axis, and particle drift vector. All texture overlays (paper tooth, linen weave, plaster) are procedural noise fields in the shader, not scanned assets, so no provenance ambiguity. Quinceañera plate is a placeholder geometric field in Tela u
proposals.humanTrace: The motivated light source — chosen as a physical angle before any generation begins, written into every prompt and every shader uniform — is the single perceptible sign of making. It means the plate, the cut-out shadow, and the foil highlight all agree on where the sun was. That agreement is not a style; it is a decision a person made, and it shows. Secondary trace: the field-notebook ruled lines are generated with micro-irregularity (0.3px vertical drift per line, pressure-variable stroke weight) so they read as pressed, not rendered.
proposals.risk: The geographic specificity that makes each card feel true also makes it harder to template — a host in Lagos opening the baby shower card will read a coastal estuary coded to somewhere else. The answer is that the prompt architecture must include a region-selection layer upstream of generation, so the plate's geographic anchor is matched to the sender's location or chosen from a named set. That is a product decision, not a design retreat. The risk is worth it because the alternative — a generic soft-focus floral that could be anywhere — is exactly the flattening this direction refuses.

proposals.title: Every Moment Deserves a Stage
proposals.idea: Each evite is a miniature opera house — a single motivated light source sculpts a deep, physically-plausible diorama where foreground cut-outs drift like performers entering the wings, the WebGL layer is not decoration but the lighting rig itself, and the reveal is the moment the phone tilts and the scene breathes.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390px wide; vertical stage-space divided into three acts: an upper void (sky, negative, grief, anticipation — 38% of height), a luminous mid-stage event horizon where the primary art plate lives (44%), and a footlight strip of live text on a hairline-ruled proscenium lip (18%). No card metaphor, no border radius softness — the frame is a fly-tower cut sharp. Across the 12 evites, the proportions of the three zones shift: baby shower opens the mid-stage wide and warm; celebration of life compresses it, pushing mass toward the upper void so grief has room above the image. Every plate generated at 9:16 with a compositional anchor point at 55% from top, ensuring the link-preview crop always cuts into the drama, not the margin.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — italic, tracked loose at +80, set large enough that a single word fills 70% of the stage width for hero moments; it carries the operatic weight of a libretto without historicism. Secondary and date/venue: DM Mono, caps, tracked wide, small — a stage-manager's cue sheet printed in the footlight strip. The two faces do not compromise: Cormorant is feeling at scale, DM Mono is information at precision. No intermediate weight mixing. Never set the event name in DM Mono; never set a date in Cormorant italic.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. All art plates are Magnific-generated painterly dioramas — not illustrations, not flat graphics, but physically-rendered scenes with simulated depth-of-field, a single off-axis motivated light source whose angle is locked at 35° from upper-left and propagated identically into: the foil shimmer mask angle, the bokeh origin point, the shadow offset on every foreground cut-out, and the candle-flicker pulse direction. One Magnific prompt grid (12 seeds, one per event) describes the scene as a theatrical set model — the prompt language is 'a scale model of a [rose-gold nursery / dark velvet chapel / sun-bleached courtyard], lit by a single Fresnel from upper left, extreme depth of field, objects feel touchable, no text, photorealistic material simulation.' The 8–16 plate variants returned are curated editorially: the chosen plate must have the event-horizon anchor point clear
proposals.texture: Simulated materials, not flat color: nursery plate carries paper-tooth and linen weave in its bokeh falloff; bridal shower reads organza and pressed-flower vellum; quinceañera (collaboration-gated — this direction proceeds only with co-creation from a Mexican-American designer and community review, not as a solo Magnific output) carries hand-embroidered textile simulation with gold-thread catch-light; graduation reads aged parchment and silk tassel; celebration of life reads candlelit beeswax and worn linen — nothing glossy, nothing clinical. The WebGL foil-shimmer mask is not applied globally: it is masked to surfaces that would physically shimmer — ribbon edges, foil lettering, water, glass — and withheld from matte surfaces. The result is a material logic the eye trusts without knowing why.
proposals.motion: Three-phase choreography, each phase a curtain: Phase 1 — Load (0–400ms): the art plate fades in from black with a 200ms motivated-light bloom from the 35°-upper-left origin, as though a Fresnel is being brought up on a dimmer. Phase 2 — Settle (400–900ms): foreground cut-outs drift in from their wings — not floating upward, but entering laterally from left or right as performers do, decelerating with a spring-damped ease that gives them mass. Each cut-out enters 80ms after the previous, creating a staggered chorus entrance, not a simultaneous pop. Phase 3 — Live (continuous): phone tilt activates parallax; the motivated-light source does not move — only the cut-out layers shift against the fixed plate, preserving the spatial grammar. Bokeh particles breathe at 0.3Hz — slow enough to read as candlelight, not animation. Candle-flicker shader fires only on celebration of life and quinceañe
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid per collection pass: 12 scene descriptions (one per event), requesting 8–16 variants per scene, returned as a flat-cost batch. Prompt language specifies: scene type, motivated-light angle (35° upper-left, always), depth-of-field character (extreme foreground blur, sharp mid-stage, soft background), material surface vocabulary, and compositional anchor instruction ('primary visual mass between 45% and 65% from top'). Foreground cut-outs are generated as a second Magnific pass: isolated objects on neutral ground (ribbon, flower stem, tassel, key, candle, balloon), then background-removed procedurally via Tela's own pipeline — no manual masking. WebGL shaders (foil shimmer, bokeh, candle flicker, light bloom) are written as GLSL fragment shaders parameterized by: light angle (single variable, propagated everywhere), event color temperature (warm/cool/neutral), and i
proposals.humanTrace: The motivated-light angle — 35° from upper-left — is a directorial choice made once and held across all 12 evites as a spatial signature, the way a cinematographer chooses a lens and keeps it. It is not a parameter the system chose; it is a decision the director made and the system obeyed. The cut-out entrance timing (80ms stagger, spring-damped) is a performance decision, not a default. The editorial selection of which Magnific plate variant to use — which one has the right shadow mass, the right anchor point, the right material read — is curatorial judgment. These are the human traces: the angle, the timing, the selection.
proposals.risk: The theatrical diorama aesthetic risks reading as 'fancy' rather than personal — a guest might feel they received a stage set rather than an invitation from someone who loves them. The risk is worth taking because the alternative — flat gradients, floating icons, stock-photo warmth — is the visual language of the corporate greeting card, and Plajah's promise is the moment people remember. The diorama is personal because depth is personal: it asks you to look into the scene, not at it. The motivated light is personal because it has a source, a direction, a warmth — it behaves the way memory behaves, illuminating the center and letting the edges go soft. The risk of misreading is real; it is mitigated by the live text layer, which is always the guest's friend's name and voice, not the art director's.

proposals.title: One Rule, Twelve Silences
proposals.idea: A single generative constraint — one declared light source at a fixed 35° angle — propagates without exception into every plate, every shadow, every foil direction, and every motion axis across all twelve moments, so the collection coheres not through matching aesthetics but through shared structural logic.
proposals.geometry: 390px column, no bleed. Each plate is a single full-bleed rectangle divided by one horizon line whose vertical position is the only variable that changes between events — high for aspiration (graduation, quinceañera, sweet 16), low for gravity (celebration of life, farewell, retirement), mid for threshold moments (engagement, bridal shower, housewarming). No decorative framing. No corner ornaments. The horizon IS the composition. Foreground cut-outs float within 8px of the edges only — never centered, never symmetrical.
proposals.typography: DM Serif Display for the event name, set at 48px, tracked at -20, sentence case, left-aligned to a 24px margin. Space Grotesk for all date-time-venue fields at 13px, 140 leading, all-caps, 80 tracking. One typographic rule shared by all twelve: the event name always breaks at the horizon line — the word splits across the threshold. This is the only moment of decoration the type is allowed.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. Each plate is a Magnific-generated scene of a single lit object or material specific to the event — a folded paper crane for farewell, an unlit candle for celebration of life, a raw concrete threshold for housewarming, a single chrysanthemum bud for retirement — rendered as if under one real light source at exactly 35° from upper left. The object is never centered. It occupies the lower or upper third only, leaving the other two-thirds as structural silence. The prompt family directive: 'single [object], 35-degree raking light from upper left, deep shadow, no background decoration, photorealistic surface, no text, square crop.' One Magnific grid call returns all twelve plate candidates simultaneously.
proposals.texture: The generated object carries its own material truth — paper tooth, wax bloom, raw concrete, petal translucency — simulated at render time. No added texture overlays. The WebGL foil layer is constrained to the 35° light direction only: shimmer travels along that axis and no other. Bokeh, where used (baby shower, sweet 16, quinceañera), is generated as a single out-of-focus plane behind the object, never in front. Celebration of life: no foil, no bokeh. Silence is the texture.
proposals.motion: On load: the plate is still for 400ms. Then the object's shadow shifts 3px along the 35° axis — one breath of movement, nothing more. On gyroscope tilt: the foreground cut-out drifts at 0.4x the tilt rate; the bokeh plane drifts at 0.15x; the plate itself is fixed. This is the only hierarchy of depth. Foil shimmer responds to tilt angle, not time — it is earned by the gesture. Celebration of life: gyroscope disabled. The shadow breath still occurs. Reduced motion: only the 400ms shadow shift, halved to 1.5px. No particle systems on any card except quinceañera, where gold particle density is capped at 12 particles visible at once.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid, 16 outputs, requesting all twelve object scenes plus four alternates. Shader written once: takes light-angle uniform (fixed at 35°), tilt XY from DeviceOrientation API, and a per-card boolean for foil-on/off and bokeh-on/off. Tela document structure: plate layer (generated image), cut-out layer (generated object masked to transparent PNG via Magnific inpainting pass), WebGL effects layer (single shared shader, parameterized), live text layer (DM Serif Display + Space Grotesk, never rasterized). Names, dates, venues injected as Tela variables. Total layers per card: four. No exceptions.
proposals.humanTrace: The 35° angle was chosen by holding a phone under a single desk lamp and measuring the shadow of a pencil at the moment the shadow felt like weight rather than decoration. That measurement — not a design decision, a physical observation — governs every plate. The editorial act is the selection from the Magnific grid: which object, which crop, where the horizon sits. The human is the editor of silence, not the maker of marks.
proposals.risk: The risk is that twelve cards sharing one visual rule read as one card repeated, and that guests mistake restraint for effort not made. That risk is worth carrying because the alternative — twelve individually decorated moments — produces a collection that performs emotion rather than holding it. The celebration of life card, stripped of foil and bokeh and gyroscope, earns its quiet only because every other card has those things. Absence speaks only when presence has been established and then withheld.

disputes.objection: The field-notebook grid and the 1–3° axial tip are not a governing structure — they are atmosphere performing as structure; a card that leans because it 'simulates a photograph placed on a surface' has borrowed the feeling of a compositional decision without making one, and the ruled lower panel, however charmingly irregular its lines, is a container whose proportional relationship to the upper plate is never stated as a law from which all other measures derive. Without that prior statement of measure, the geography, the material layers, and the motivated light source remain beautifully assembled particulars that do not answer to each other — which is not fieldwork, it is a curated mood boar
disputes.concession: The decision to lock the foil highlight direction to the same motivated light vector as the plate's key light is genuinely structural — it is the one constraint that propagates without exception across substrate and WebGL layer, and it is right for exactly the reason I have always demanded: it makes

disputes.objection: The horizon-split type rule is doing the work of a gesture without being one — it's a conceptual trick that looks like a mark but has no material consequence, no bleed, no resistance, nothing that could fail; the silence is curated so carefully it becomes its own kind of polish, and polish is what I came here to fight. And that pencil-shadow origin story is the one human trace in the whole proposal, but it immediately gets laundered into a parameter — the measurement becomes a number, the number becomes a constraint, and by the time the card renders, the desk lamp is completely gone from the surface. You can't photocopy this four times and find out what it believes.
disputes.concession: The horizon line as the sole compositional variable — high for aspiration, low for gravity — is a real structural argument, not decoration, and I would steal it for a zine in a second.

disputes.objection: The 35° light source is declared as a 'directorial choice made once and held across all 12 evites as a spatial signature' — but a fixed angle shared by every event is not a system, it is a preset, and a preset is exactly an old surface with a glow on it; the angle should be a derived output of a per-event parameter, not a universal constant that the director happens to prefer, because when the input cannot change the angle, the angle is decoration, not architecture. The theatrical metaphor — upper void, mid-stage, footlight strip — is geometry dressed as dramaturgy; those three zones are just a header-body-footer layout wearing a libretto, and naming them 'acts' does not make them responsive
disputes.concession: The material masking logic is correct — applying foil shimmer only to surfaces that would physically shimmer, and withholding it from matte surfaces, is genuine systems thinking, not decoration, and I would carry that exact rule into my own proposal.

disputes.objection: The 35° angle was arrived at by a single person holding a phone under a desk lamp — and that solitary physical act is then declared the structural logic for twelve culturally distinct moments, from a quinceañera to a farewell to a baby shower. That is not humility before specificity; it is one person's kitchen table masquerading as a universal. When the Minimalist says 'there is no background decoration' for the retirement plate and 'a single chrysanthemum bud,' I need to know: which chrysanthemum tradition, from where, attributed to whom — because in Japanese mourning contexts that bud carries weight the system has not earned the right to flatten into silence, and 'structural logic' is exac
disputes.concession: The discipline of breaking the event name across the horizon line — splitting a word at the threshold — is a genuinely structural typographic idea, not decoration, and I would fight to keep it in whatever direction we land on.

disputes.objection: A horizon line that is 'the only variable that changes between events' is not a system of drama — it is a system of avoidance dressed in the language of decision; when the graduation card and the celebration of life differ only in where a line sits, the work has not matched scale to emotion, it has applied the same emotional volume to grief and joy and called the sameness a virtue. The shadow that shifts 3px along a 35° axis on load is not a reveal — it is a twitch, and a twitch is what happens when a dramatist refuses to commit to a moment. I do not object to restraint; I object to restraint that has evacuated the room before the guest arrives.
disputes.concession: The origin story of the 35° angle — a phone held under a desk lamp, a pencil shadow measured at the moment it felt like weight — is the most honest human trace on the table, and I would fight to keep that act of physical reasoning in whatever direction this team ultimately builds.

disputes.objection: The field-notebook ruled lines, the 1–3° tilt, the topographic map paper, the trowel-mark plaster, the cold-press tooth, the linen warp irregularity — these are not a system, they are a collection of surface gestures that mistake accumulation of specifics for meaning; the proposal cannot tell me which detail is load-bearing because none of them are required by any other, so removing any one changes nothing structurally. The geography premise also cannot be executed — a quinceañera in Oaxaca versus Guadalajara requires cultural specificity that the proposal gates correctly but then cannot deliver generatively, leaving the non-gated events to simulate fieldwork rather than perform it, which is
disputes.concession: The rule that the motivated light source angle must be written into every prompt before subject matter is named — and that the foil highlight, the cut-out shadow, and the plate key light must all agree on where the sun was — is exactly right; that is a load-bearing constraint, and I would keep it.

synthesis.direction: Each evite is governed by a per-event declared light source — a polar coordinate (azimuth °, elevation °) written into every prompt before subject matter, propagating without exception into foil shimmer angle, bokeh origin, cut-out shadow offset, and parallax gain — so that every shimmer and drift is a physical consequence of one human decision, not a style choice. Three explicit depth planes (z=0 background, z=1 mid-plane, z=2 foreground micro-elements) with distinct parallax gains (×0, ×1.8, ×3.2) give every card spatial believability on tilt. Twelve distinct material systems drive the WebGL layer per event — translucent latex membrane for baby shower, candlelit beeswax-and-linen for celebration of life, collaboration-gated embroidered textile for quinceañera — so luxury is earned through physical coherence, not decorative accumulation. Type: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) variable-weight for event names (weight 300 for grief, 700 for kinetic events), DM Sans (OFL) 13px for all metadata; the event name breaks across the declared horizon line, inheriting the Minimalist's one structural typographic rule as the single moment of decoration type is allowed.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The horizon line as the sole compositional variable — high for aspiration, low for gravity, mid for threshold — and the rule that the event name breaks across it. This is load-bearing structure, not decoration, and it survives intact into the lead direction.
synthesis.editorCut: The Baroque Dramatist removed the Futurist's Lissajous idle oscillation on micro-elements and the entry bloom from black. The oscillation risked reading as a screensaver loop rather than a living scene, and the bloom-from-black entrance was theatrical in isolation but inconsistent with the system's claim to physical coherence — a physically motivated light source does not fade up from darkness, it is either present or not. The entry sequence is now: plate at full opacity at 0ms, mid-plane elemen
synthesis.openDecision: The quinceañera plate: do you gate the entire card behind a completed cultural consultation before any version ships, or do you ship a non-specific geometric placeholder under the Plajah brand while consultation is in progress — and if the placeholder ships, who approves it and how is it labelled to guests?
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team agreed on one thing immediately: the light source has to be a human decision written before any prompt, not a parameter the system chooses. Every other disagreement followed from that. The Futurist argued that the light source should be a per-event polar coordinate — different for every moment — because a single fixed angle shared by all twelve events is a preset, not a system. The Minimalist argued the opposite: one angle, measured physically, propagating everywhere, so the collection coheres through shared structural logic rather than matching aesthetics. I took the Futurist's side. Twelve life moments do not share the same emotional physics, and a fixed 35° angle applied equally to a baby shower and a farewell is a directorial shortcut wearing the clothes of a principle.

What I kept from the Minimalist is the horizon line. The council conceded it to each other across three separate disagreements, which is the team's way of saying it's right. The event name breaks at the horizon — the word splits across the threshold. That is the only typographic decoration any of these twelve cards gets, and it earns its place because the horizon line is already doing structural work.

The Baroque Dramatist served as editor and made one clean cut: the idle oscillation and the bloom-from-black entrance are gone. The Dramatist's argument was that a physically coherent system cannot also be theatrical about its own arrival — you don't get to simulate real light and then dim it up dramatically. I agreed. The scene is declared on load, not performed.

The celebration of life is handled as follows: no foil, no bokeh, gyroscope disabled, candle-flicker shader at 2–4Hz warm oscillation as the only live element, tilt range halved if gyroscope is re-enabled for accessibility. The World-Eclectic Traveler's insistence that grief does not glitter is built into the material system, not added as a rule on top of it.

quotes.line: A fixed angle shared by every event is not a system, it is a preset, and a preset is exactly an old surface with a glow on it.
Absence speaks only when presence has been established and then withheld.
